newsitem.title: USA: Florida population hits 14.7 mln, but growth slows.
newsitem.headline: Florida population hits 14.7 mln, but growth slows.

text.p: Florida's population has risen to 14.7 million, a gain of 1.76 million people or 13.6 percent since 1990, the Universtiy of Florida said Thursday.

The population a year ago was 14.1 million, according to university researchers, who produce official data used by the legislature to distribute state funds to cities and counties, representing a population gain of two percent for the year.
Florida's population growth has eased since the 1970s and 1980s because of a slowdown in the retiree influx and a decline in births.

"But growth has been stronger in the last few years than during the early '90s when a severe recession slowed migration to the state," said Stanley Smith, director of population studies for the school's Bureau of Economic and Business Research.
Four of Florida's six largest counties had population gains of more than 100,000 since 1990.
Broward County led with 164,178 new residents in seven years, followed by Palm Beach County with 140,181, Dade County with 133,379 and Orange County with 125,897 new residents.
Hillsborough County gained 94,499 residents and Pinellas County gained 36,482 duringthe period.
Lafayette, Franklin, Holmes and Calhoun counties had the smallest gains, with fewer than 2,000 new residents each since 1990.
Palm Beach County's population passed the 1 million mark during the year, as did that of the Jacksonville-Duval County area.
Counties with the fastest growth rates however, were smaller ones. Flager County's population grew by 43.51 percent, followed by Sumter County at 40.5 percent and Liberty County at 36.95 percent.
By contrast, Pinellas, Dade, Putnam and Monroe counties saw growth rates of less than 8 perent since 1990.
